# Behavioral Specification: Alert Handler Register Access and Mapping Module

## 1. Overview

This module provides the register-access layer for an alert handler. It presents the software-visible register set on a bus slave interface and connects those register contents to the alert-handler logic. It also generates the four alert-class interrupts and maintains the sideband crashdump output.

The module does not perform alert classification, escalation policy decisions, ping generation, or low-power management. Its responsibility is to:

- expose configuration and status registers to software,
- update status registers from alert-handler activity,
- provide configuration values to the alert-handler logic,
- generate class interrupts from class-trigger events and interrupt control state,
- produce a latching crashdump snapshot,
- report register-file integrity errors.

## 2. Reset Behavior

On reset, the module must return all state to its reset default:

- all interrupt status must be cleared,
- all interrupt outputs must be deasserted,
- all configuration, status, cause, threshold, and counter registers must take their reset values,
- no crashdump snapshot may be latched,
- the crashdump output must reflect the current reset state,
- any shadowed-register errors and bus-integrity alert outputs must be deasserted.

## 3. Bus and Register Access

Software must be able to access all implemented alert-handler registers through the bus interface using the access semantics defined for each register.

The module must honor register lock behavior:

- once a configuration write-enable is cleared, further software writes to the associated configuration register must have no effect,
- locked configuration values must remain stable until reset,
- shadowed registers must only update when the required shadowed write protocol is satisfied.

If a shadowed register storage mismatch or shadowed update error is detected, the module must assert the corresponding internal error indication to the alert-handler logic. These indications are events intended to be treated as local alert sources.

If a bus integrity error is detected, the module must assert the fatal integrity alert output.

## 4. Interrupt Generation

The module must generate one interrupt per alert class.

For each class:

- a class-trigger event must set the corresponding interrupt status,
- software writing the interrupt test bit must also set the interrupt status,
- software clearing the interrupt status must clear it,
- the interrupt output must be asserted only when the interrupt status is set and the interrupt enable is set,
- the interrupt status must be set by a trigger event even if the interrupt enable is not set.

## 5. Cause Register Updates

The module must maintain a sticky cause bit for every external alert and every local alert.

When the alert-handler logic indicates that an alert cause event has occurred, the corresponding cause bit must be set. Once set, a cause bit must remain set until software clears it.

The current cause-bit values must be exposed to the alert-handler logic and must be included in the crashdump state.

## 6. Configuration Outputs to Alert-Handler Logic

The module must continuously provide the following configuration information to the alert-handler logic:

- whether the ping timer is enabled,
- the ping timeout value,
- for each external alert:
  - whether the alert is enabled,
  - which class it is assigned to,
  - whether it is eligible for ping testing,
- for each local alert:
  - whether it is enabled,
  - which class it is assigned to,
- for each class:
  - whether the class is enabled,
  - which escalation signals are enabled,
  - the phase-to-escalation-signal mapping,
  - the accumulated-alert threshold,
  - the interrupt timeout value,
  - the duration of each escalation phase,
  - the phase at which a crashdump should be latched.

An external alert must be considered eligible for ping testing only when that alert is both enabled and locked. An alert is locked when its configuration write-enable has been cleared.

A class must be considered enabled only when its master enable is set and at least one of its escalation-signal enables is set.

## 7. Class Clear and Auto-Lock Behavior

The module must provide a class-clear indication whenever a class clear register is written with 1.

If a class is enabled, has its lock bit set, and its escalation protocol is triggered, the module must disable the software write-enable of that class's clear register. This must prevent software from clearing the class escalation state once escalation has begun.

Until such a lock condition applies, software must be able to clear the class accumulation counter, escalation counter, and escalation state by writing the class clear register.

## 8. Current Counter and State Visibility

The module must continuously update the software-readable status registers with the current values supplied by the alert-handler logic:

- current accumulation counts for each class,
- current escalation counts for each class,
- current escalation state for each class.

These values must be observable through the bus interface at all times.

## 9. Crashdump Output

The crashdump output must provide a snapshot of selected alert-handler state.

Before any latch event, the crashdump output must continuously reflect the current state:

- all external alert cause bits,
- all local alert cause bits,
- current accumulation counts,
- current escalation counts,
- current escalation state.

When the crashdump latch request is asserted and no snapshot has been latched since reset or since the last re-arm, the module must capture the current state and hold it constant on the crashdump output.

After a snapshot has been latched, further assertions of the latch request must not overwrite the latched snapshot.

The latched snapshot must be discarded, and the crashdump mechanism re-armed, when any class-clear indication is generated. After re-arming, the crashdump output must again follow the current state until the next latch request.

On reset, the latch state must be cleared and the crashdump output must follow the current state.

## 10. Error Reporting

The module must report errors as follows:

- a shadowed-register storage error must be reported as an internal error event,
- a shadowed-register update error must be reported as an internal error event,
- a bus-integrity error must be reported on the fatal integrity alert output.

These error indications must remain inactive when no corresponding error is present, and must be distinguishable from one another so that the alert-handler logic can classify them appropriately.

# Behavioral Specification: Alert Handler Register Wrapper

## 1. Overview

This module provides the register-access layer for the alert handler. It is responsible for:

- Exposing a memory-mapped bus interface for software to configure and read alert-handler state.
- Generating one interrupt output per alert class.
- Translating programmed register values into configuration outputs for the alert-handler hardware.
- Receiving hardware event and status information and updating the corresponding status registers.
- Producing a crashdump snapshot that can be latched for later retrieval by hardware debug or recovery logic.

The module does not itself perform alert classification, escalation, or ping generation. It provides the configuration and status interface required by those functions.

## 2. Reset Behavior

- All state in the module must be reset to its defined reset value when the primary reset is asserted.
- Shadowed registers shall have a dedicated shadow reset. When the shadow reset is asserted, shadowed register storage shall be held in its reset state and not accept updates.
- After reset, all interrupts must be deasserted, all interrupt state bits must be cleared, and all alert enables must default to disabled.
- Configuration lock registers shall reset to their unlocked/reset state so that software can perform initial configuration.

## 3. Bus Register Interface

The module shall act as a device on the system bus and must:

- Accept valid bus read and write transactions and return appropriate bus responses.
- Decode incoming transactions to the correct register addresses.
- Implement read, write, write-to-clear, and hardware-update semantics as defined by the register map.
- Preserve read-only status registers from software writes.
- Ignore writes to locked registers.
- Support shadowed-register behavior for critical configuration fields, including shadow reset and update semantics.
- Report shadowed-register storage and update errors through status outputs.
- Assert the bus integrity alert output when a bus transaction fails an integrity check.

The module must never allow a software write to change a locked configuration value. Locked values shall remain stable until the next reset.

## 4. Interrupt Generation

There shall be one interrupt output for each alert class: Class A, Class B, Class C, and Class D.

For each class interrupt:

- The interrupt output must be asserted when both the class interrupt state bit is set and the corresponding interrupt enable bit is set.
- A hardware class-event indication shall set the corresponding interrupt state bit.
- If a hardware event arrives while the state bit is already set, the state bit shall remain set.
- The interrupt state bit shall be set even if the interrupt enable bit is cleared; the output is asserted only when enabled.
- Software shall be able to clear the interrupt state bit by writing 1 to it.
- A write of 1 to the interrupt test register shall set the corresponding interrupt state bit, allowing software to verify interrupt behavior.
- Clearing the interrupt state bit shall deassert the interrupt output, assuming the enable bit remains set.

## 5. Alert Configuration Outputs

### 5.1 Per-Alert Configuration

For every alert source, the module shall make the following configuration values available to the hardware:

- Whether the alert is enabled.
- Which class the alert is assigned to.
- Whether the alert is eligible for ping testing.

An alert shall be considered ping-eligible only when it is both enabled and locked. Enabled-but-unlocked alerts must not be pinged, because they may still be reconfigured or disabled by software.

### 5.2 Local Alert Configuration

For each locally sourced alert, the module shall expose:

- Whether the local alert is enabled.
- Which class the local alert is assigned to.

Local alerts shall follow the same class-assignment behavior as external alerts.

### 5.3 Ping Configuration

The module shall expose:

- The ping timer enable configuration.
- The ping timeout cycle count.

These values shall be taken directly from the corresponding software-programmed registers.

## 6. Class Configuration Outputs

### 6.1 Class Enable

A class shall be considered enabled when both of the following conditions are true:

- The class’s main enable bit is set.
- At least one of the four escalation-signal enable bits for that class is set.

If the main enable is set but all escalation-signal enables are cleared, the class shall be treated as disabled.

### 6.2 Escalation Configuration

For each class, the module shall expose:

- The four escalation-signal enable bits.
- The mapping from each escalation phase to the escalation signal that should be activated during that phase.
- The duration of each escalation phase.
- The accumulation threshold for the class.
- The interrupt timeout cycle count for the class.

### 6.3 Class Clear and Autolock Behavior

Software shall be able to clear a class accumulator and stop its escalation sequence by writing 1 to the class clear register, provided clearing is permitted.

The module shall implement an autolock behavior as follows:

- If a class has its lock bit set and is enabled, and the hardware indicates that this class has triggered escalation, the module shall automatically clear that class’s clear-enable register.
- Once the clear-enable register is cleared in this way, software must not be able to clear the class accumulator or stop the escalation sequence through the class clear register.
- This behavior prevents software from interrupting an escalation once it has begun, when the configuration requires escalation to be unstoppable.

## 7. Status Register Updates

### 7.1 Alert Cause Registers

For each external alert source:

- When the hardware indicates that the alert has occurred, the corresponding sticky cause bit must be set to 1.
- If the cause bit is already 1, it shall remain 1.
- Software shall be able to clear the cause bit by writing 1 to it.

For each locally sourced alert:

- The same sticky-cause behavior shall apply.

### 7.2 Class Status Registers

The module shall continuously update the following status registers from live hardware state:

- The current accumulator count for each class.
- The current escalation counter for each class.
- The current escalation state for each class.

These status values shall be readable by software and shall not be directly writable by software.

### 7.3 Class Clear Pulses

When software writes 1 to a class clear register, the module shall generate a clear request for that class. This request shall be presented to the hardware only if the class clear is permitted by the clear-enable and lock state.

## 8. Crashdump Output

The crashdump output shall contain:

- The current sticky cause status for all external alert sources.
- The current sticky cause status for all locally sourced alerts.
- The current class accumulator counts.
- The current class escalation counters.
- The current class escalation states.

The crashdump output shall operate in two modes: live mode and latched mode.

### 8.1 Live Mode

After reset and after re-arming, the crashdump output shall present the live status values described above. Changes in alert cause registers and class status shall be reflected at the output as they occur.

### 8.2 Latching Behavior

When the crashdump latch request is asserted, and the crashdump mechanism is not already latched, the module shall capture the current crashdump data and hold it on the output.

Once latched:

- The output shall remain constant.
- Subsequent changes to live alert cause registers or class status shall not affect the output.
- The latch request shall not cause a second capture while data is already latched.

### 8.3 Re-Arming

The crashdump mechanism shall be re-armed whenever any class clear register is written with 1.

When re-armed:

- The previously latched snapshot shall be discarded.
- The output shall return to live mode.
- A later latch request shall be able to capture a new snapshot.

If a class clear and a latch request occur at the same time, the clear shall take priority, and a new capture shall not begin until the next cycle in which the latch request is still asserted.

## 9. Error Indications

The module shall provide error indications for the following conditions:

- An integrity error is detected on the bus interface.
- A shadowed register reports a storage error.
- A shadowed register reports an update error.

These error indications shall be exposed as outputs and shall be suitable for use as alert conditions by the surrounding hardware.

## 10. Summary of Required Behavior

In summary, the module shall:

- Provide a correct, software-accessible register interface for the alert handler.
- Generate four class interrupts using standard interrupt enable/state/test semantics.
- Forward alert, local-alert, ping, and class configuration to the alert handler hardware.
- Keep status and cause registers updated from hardware events.
- Enforce locking and autolock behavior.
- Provide a crashdump snapshot with latching and re-arming behavior.
- Report shadowed-register and bus-integrity errors.

These behaviors shall be maintained regardless of the number of alert sources configured at build time.
